implementation_statement: Access control policy POL-02 and standards STD-02.1 to STD-02.3 (P06) apply to the ECIS. Procedures PRC-02.1 to PRC-02.4 cover provisioning, certification, privileged access, and break-glass access.

Workforce EHR accounts are provisioned by identity governance from HR and credentialing events using role templates approved by the Chief Nursing Officer and Chief Medical Information Officer. Agency and contracted staff accounts carry end dates from the staffing system. Gaps: 4 of 60 sampled departures (all agency or contracted) were disabled 2 to 9 days late, and 23% of about 1,150 service accounts are not vaulted (POAM-001; POAM-002).
evidence: EV-004 (identity governance role templates); EV-009 (EHR user export); EV-AC-2 (P07 AC-2 results)

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Joiner, mover, and leaver events flow from the HR system and the medical staff credentialing system to identity governance, which provisions and removes EHR roles through the SSO connector.

Workforce accounts inactive for 60 days are disabled automatically. SL-1 affiliate accounts are managed by practice administrators; 214 affiliate accounts inactive more than 90 days were still enabled at assessment (POAM-015).
evidence: EV-004 (inactivity job report); EV-008 (affiliate account export)

implementation_statement: EHR security classes enforce role-based access to activities and record types. Part 2 records from the H-03 program carry a sensitive-record flag that limits access, with gaps in consistent flagging (see SC-4 and POAM-021). Break-the-glass access to restricted records requires a reason and is reviewed by the Privacy Office.
evidence: EV-009 (EHR security class matrix; break-the-glass report)

implementation_statement: Network policy limits flows to the EHR database tier to the application tier and the integration engine; interface flows are defined per channel on the integration engine. Enterprise network segmentation is provided by CCP-05.
evidence: EV-014 (firewall rule review); EV-059 (interface channel inventory)

implementation_statement: Role design separates EHR build (order sets, drug database, security classes) from production migration, and separates security class administration from clinical roles. Build changes are migrated by the change team, not the builder.
Least privilege is enforced through role templates and quarterly certification. Database and server administrators hold no standing privileges; access is granted just in time through PAM.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: All privileged sessions to ECIS servers and databases run through PAM with session recording forwarded to the SIEM.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: SSO locks accounts after 10 failed attempts in 15 minutes; badge-tap workstations require the PIN after lock. The patient portal locks after 6 failed attempts.
evidence: EV-002 (SSO lockout configuration); EV-075 (portal lockout configuration)

implementation_statement: The EHR and remote access gateways display an approved notice on sign-in that use is monitored and limited to authorized purposes.
The EHR limits each user to one concurrent session per device class; clinical roaming sessions follow the badge.
Clinical workstations lock after 10 minutes, or immediately on badge tap-out; non-clinical workstations lock after 15 minutes. Locked screens hide patient information.
EHR sessions end after 30 minutes of inactivity on shared clinical workstations and 15 minutes on remote access.
evidence: EV-009 (EHR session settings); EV-016 (gateway session settings)

control_name: Permitted Actions Without Identification or Authentication
implementation_statement: No EHR function is available without identification, except the public patient portal sign-in and help pages.

Workforce and affiliate remote access to the EHR goes through the zero-trust application gateway with MFA. Vendor support for the EHR uses PAM. Gap: three analyzer and device platforms that feed the ECIS still use vendor remote tools outside PAM (POAM-011).
evidence: EV-016 (gateway configuration; PAM vendor sessions); EV-AC-17 (P07 AC-17 results)

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: Remote sessions are protected with TLS 1.2 or higher through the zero-trust gateway and the PAM gateway.
Hospital wireless uses enterprise authentication with certificates for clinical devices and workstations on wheels; guest wireless is isolated from the clinical network.

Mobile devices that access the EHR (clinician phones and tablets) are enrolled in mobile device management with encryption and remote wipe; the EHR mobile app stores no data at rest outside its container.
Use of personal and external systems is limited by STD-05.2: personal devices only through the EHR mobile app or the zero-trust gateway; no PHI on unmanaged storage.
Release of information and HIE sharing follow the Privacy Office's rules; Part 2 records require consent checks before any disclosure (42 CFR Part 2).
Content on public websites and portal help pages is reviewed before posting so that no PHI is published.
Training policy and STD-05.1 apply to all ECIS users.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Annual security and privacy training and quarterly phishing exercises for the workforce, including employed physicians and agency staff before first shift. 96% completion for 2026.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Role-based training for EHR users at go-live and with upgrades; downtime and BCA training is required annually for charge nurses and ED staff, but completion is 71% and no training covers multi-hospital downtime (POAM-016).
evidence: EV-036 (learning system report; downtime competency records); EV-AT-3 (P07 AT-3 results)

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Training records are kept in the learning system for 6 years.
Audit logging standard STD-01.4 applies to the ECIS.

The EHR logs sign-in, record access, break-the-glass, order and result events, prescription of controlled substances, security class changes, and build migrations. The selection is reviewed annually by the Privacy Office and SOC.
EHR audit records include user, workstation, patient, activity, date and time, and outcome.
The SIEM and log archive are sized for 13 months online and 6 years in the archive, with capacity alerts at 75%.

control_name: Response to Audit Logging Process Failures
implementation_statement: The SIEM alerts the SOC within 15 minutes if an ECIS log source stops sending.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The SOC reviews ECIS security events daily using SIEM correlation, and the Privacy Office reviews access reports (VIP, employee, and same-name records) weekly. Gaps: the H-08 legacy EHR (outside this boundary but connected through the integration engine) and medical device gateways do not feed the SIEM (POAM-007).
evidence: EV-087 (SOC review records); EV-037 (Privacy Office reports); EV-AU-6 (P07 AU-6 results)

implementation_statement: Audit review is automated through SIEM correlation rules and the privacy monitoring tool; findings open cases automatically.

control_name: Audit Record Reduction and Report Generation
implementation_statement: The SIEM and privacy monitoring tool support search and report generation without changing the original records.
ECIS servers and network devices synchronize to internal time sources traced to an authoritative source.
Logs are forwarded to a write-once archive in a separate account; ECIS administrators cannot delete them.

control_name: Store on Separate Physical Systems or Components
implementation_statement: A copy of ECIS audit logs is stored in the cloud log archive account, separate from the data centers.

Electronic signatures in the EHR bind each note, order, and result verification to the authenticated user, and signed entries cannot be changed without an addendum that records who and when (42 CFR 482.24(c)(1)).
ECIS logs are kept 13 months online and 6 years in the archive.
Audit generation is enabled on all EHR application, database, and integration engine components; changes to audit settings are themselves logged.
STD-01.2 (security assessment and system authorization) applies to the ECIS.
Internal Audit assesses the ECIS annually under SP 800-53A Rev. 5 (P07).
Assessors are Internal Audit staff with no role in designing or operating the controls.

Each external connection (affiliate practices, HIEs, reference laboratory, state health departments, clearinghouses, H-08) has an interface or interconnection agreement listing data, security terms, and contacts. The H-08 connection agreement is interim (POAM-006).
Weaknesses are tracked in the POA&M in the GRC platform with owners and dates (P07 poam.csv).
The Chief Operating Officer, as authorizing official equivalent, decided on 2026-08-24 to continue operation with conditions (section 4.2).
Continuous monitoring reports monthly metrics (patching, EDR coverage, access certification, backup success, log source health) to the executive risk committee.

An independent firm performs annual penetration testing of the ECIS external surfaces (portal, FHIR API, remote access) and an internal test from a hospital network; the 2026 test found no critical findings open beyond 30 days.
Internal connections from medical device gateways, ADC servers, and analyzer middleware are documented in the interface inventory with an owner and purpose.
STD-01.5 configuration and change management applies to the ECIS.
Baselines for EHR servers, databases, and presentation servers are defined as code and checked weekly; the EHR build baseline is versioned in the vendor's change tools.

EHR build and technical changes go through the clinical change advisory board, with medical staff approval for order sets and pharmacy approval for drug database changes. Gap: 6 of 40 sampled emergency changes lacked retrospective approval within 5 business days (POAM-012).
evidence: EV-057 (change records; CAB minutes); EV-CM-3 (P07 CM-3 results)

control_name: Testing, Validation, and Documentation of Changes
implementation_statement: Changes are tested in the vendor-provided test and training environments before migration; upgrades get a full regression test with clinical validators.
Each change records a security and clinical impact analysis; changes to clinical decision support (including SYS-15 thresholds) require Chief Medical Information Officer review.
Only the change team can migrate build to production, through PAM; developers and builders have no production write access.

Endpoint and server settings follow hardened baselines (CCP-06); EHR application security settings follow the vendor's security guide with documented deviations. Gaps: 2 of 16 device integration gateways still used vendor default settings (POAM-010), and deviations for unsupported devices that feed the ECIS are not all approved (POAM-009).
evidence: EV-011 (configuration compliance report); EV-CM-6 (P07 CM-6 results)

implementation_statement: Only required services and ports run on ECIS servers; application allow-listing runs on BCA downtime computers.
ECIS servers and BCA computers are fully inventoried in the configuration management database. Medical devices that feed the ECIS are about 88% inventoried by the discovery tool (POAM-008).
The ECIS configuration management plan defines configuration items, roles, and the release calendar.
Software licenses for the ECIS are tracked by procurement and IT asset management.
Users cannot install software on ECIS endpoints; installs go through the software catalog.
The location of ePHI in the ECIS (databases, reporting replicas, BCA caches, interface queues) is documented in the data map maintained with the Privacy Office.
STD-03.3 contingency and disaster recovery standard applies to the ECIS.

The ECIS contingency plan (v6) covers failover to DC-2, BCA downtime operations, and restoration. Gaps: it does not cover a cyber event that reaches both data centers in detail, and it does not link to IT-outage diversion criteria beyond H-01 (POAM-004; POAM-018).
evidence: EV-024 (ECIS contingency plan v6); EV-CP-2 (P07 CP-2 results)

implementation_statement: The plan is coordinated with the unified emergency preparedness program (482.15(f)), the incident response plan, and the P08 runbook.
The plan states which essential functions resume first (BIA recovery order, P05 section 8).
Data center operations and EHR technical staff complete contingency training annually.

Failover to DC-2 is tested annually (2026-03-21, 2.6 hours). A full restore from the immutable vault was tested on 2026-04-18 (41 hours). No test has combined EHR downtime at more than one hospital with diversion decisions (POAM-004).
Tests are coordinated with hospital incident command and the emergency management team.
DC-2 (colocation, Georgia) is the alternate storage site, more than 300 miles from DC-1.
DC-2 is in a different hurricane exposure zone and power grid from DC-1.
DC-2 holds a hot standby of the EHR database and application tier sized for full production load.
The alternate processing site is separated from DC-1 so that one regional event does not affect both.
Each data center and hospital has two carriers on diverse paths; clinics have cellular failover.
EHR databases are backed up nightly (full) and every 15 minutes (logs) to the immutable vault in a separate cloud account with a 35-day retention lock, and weekly to an offline copy at DC-2.
evidence: EV-019 (backup job reports; retention lock settings)

implementation_statement: Backups are restore-tested monthly for sampled databases and fully once a year.
Backup copies are kept in a separate account that ECIS administrators cannot reach, with retention locks that cannot be shortened.

Recovery runbooks exist for failover and for restore from the vault. Gap: the full restore took 41 hours against the 24-hour cyber recovery target, and the isolated recovery environment for rebuilding clean systems is not finished (POAM-003).
Transaction recovery uses database log replay to the last good point, with reconciliation of interface queues and BCA downtime records entered after recovery.
STD-02.2 identification and authentication standard applies.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Every workforce and affiliate user has a unique identity in the identity platform; clinical workstations use badge tap plus PIN for fast re-authentication.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Privileged access to ECIS servers, databases, and the EHR security tools requires phishing-resistant MFA through PAM.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Remote and affiliate access requires MFA; on-site access uses badge plus PIN as the second factor; controlled substance prescribing uses two-factor authentication in the EHR.
Medical devices and BCA computers authenticate to the network with certificates where supported; legacy devices are placed on restricted segments.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Identifiers are assigned by identity governance and never reused.

Passwords and PINs follow STD-02.2. Gaps: 23% of service accounts are not vaulted and some integration engine accounts have static passwords older than 2 years; testing found default vendor passwords on 2 clinical device integration gateways (POAM-001; POAM-010).
evidence: EV-003 (vault coverage report); EV-IA-5 (P07 IA-5 results)

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Passwords are at least 14 characters, checked against breached-password lists, with no forced periodic change.
Authentication feedback is masked in all sign-in screens.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Cryptographic modules used for authentication are FIPS 140 validated where the product supports it.

Affiliate practice users and patients are identified as non-organizational users. Affiliate users have MFA; 9 practices were found sharing logins (POAM-015). Patients use the portal with MFA offered and required for proxy access.
evidence: EV-008 (affiliate account export); EV-075 (portal settings); EV-IA-8 (P07 IA-8 results)

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Re-authentication is required after session timeout, for privileged elevation, and for signing controlled substance orders.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Workforce identity is proofed at hire through HR and credentialing; affiliate users are vouched for by their practice administrator under the hosting agreement.
Incident response policy POL-03 and its standards apply.
SOC staff, EHR technical staff, and hospital incident commanders receive incident response training annually.

The enterprise ransomware tabletop on 2026-02-26 included clinical leaders from H-01 and H-02; the next exercise (2026-11-18) adds the disclosure committee and a multi-hospital downtime drill (POAM-004; POAM-005).
Incidents follow the P08 runbook: SOC triage, EHR technical response, hospital incident command, and clinical downtime. 25 sampled incidents were handled within the standard.
Incident handling is supported by SOAR playbooks that isolate hosts and disable accounts.
Incidents are tracked in the case management system with severity, timeline, and outcome.
Workforce report suspected incidents to the service desk or SOC; the SOC escalates under STD-03.1, including to the Privacy Office for breach assessment and the General Counsel for materiality.
The SOC and the service desk give incident reporting help 24x7.

The incident response plan and P08 runbook cover the ECIS. Gap: the SEC materiality thresholds were not updated after the H-08 acquisition, and the plan has not been rehearsed with the disclosure committee and hospital incident command together (POAM-005).
evidence: EV-035 (incident response plan v5); EV-IR-8 (P07 IR-8 results)

implementation_statement: STD-01.6 maintenance standard applies.
Data center maintenance is scheduled through change control and recorded.
Maintenance tools brought into the data centers are inspected and logged.
EHR vendor remote maintenance uses PAM with approval and recording. Three device and analyzer platforms that connect to the ECIS still use vendor remote tools outside PAM (POAM-011).
Vendor maintenance staff in the data centers are escorted and their access is limited to approved work.
Support contracts give 4-hour on-site response for ECIS hardware.
STD-04.2 media protection and disposal standard applies.
Removable media is blocked on ECIS endpoints except for approved encrypted devices.
Approved removable media and printed downtime reports are labeled confidential.
Printed BCA downtime reports are kept at the nursing station and shredded when superseded; BCA computers are in staff-only areas.
Offline backup media move between data centers in locked containers with a chain-of-custody log.
Failed drives and retired equipment are sanitized under NIST SP 800-88 by a certified vendor with certificates of destruction.
Use of personal removable media is prohibited on ECIS endpoints.
STD-01.7 physical security standard applies.
Data center access lists are approved by the Director of Data Center Operations and reviewed quarterly.
DC-1 and DC-2 use badge and biometric entry, mantraps, and staffed security 24x7; hospital IT closets use badge locks.
Network cabling in data centers runs in locked cages and conduits.
Monitors and printers that show PHI in public areas are positioned or filtered to limit viewing.
Data center cameras and access alarms are monitored 24x7 and reviewed after any alarm.
Visitor records are kept for 2 years.
Power equipment and cabling are protected in restricted rooms.
Emergency power off switches are guarded and alarmed.
UPS and generators with 96 hours of fuel support DC-1; DC-2 has provider generators with 72 hours of fuel.
Emergency lighting covers data center rooms and exits.
Clean-agent fire suppression and early detection protect both data centers.
Temperature and humidity are monitored with alerts to data center operations.
Leak detection runs under raised floors and near cooling units.
Equipment deliveries and removals are logged and authorized.
Remote work with PHI follows STD-05.2: only managed devices through the gateway.
ECIS servers sit in interior rooms of DC-1 and DC-2 away from exterior walls and flood zones.
The policy hierarchy (P06 `policy-hierarchy.md`) governs planning documents.
This SSP describes the ECIS, its boundary, and its controls, and is reviewed annually.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Workforce and affiliate users accept the acceptable use policy (POL-05) at onboarding and annually.
The ECIS security architecture (tiers, data centers, gateways, backups) is described in this plan and in P04.
The ECIS uses the SP 800-53B High baseline (section 6).
Tailoring decisions (privacy controls handled by the privacy program; PM controls at enterprise level) are recorded in section 6.
Personnel security procedures in POL-01 and HR policy apply.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Positions with privileged ECIS access are designated high risk and receive enhanced screening.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Employees are background-checked before start; agency staff screening is required by contract and verified by sample.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Terminations trigger same-day disablement through identity governance. Gap: agency and contracted staff end dates depend on staffing agencies and were late in 4 of 60 samples (POAM-002).

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Transfers trigger role review within 5 business days.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Workforce sign confidentiality agreements at hire.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Staffing agency contracts require screening, training, and notice of departures within 1 business day; agencies do not always notify on time (POAM-002).
evidence: EV-006 (agency contracts); EV-004 (reconciliation reports); EV-PS-7 (P07 PS-7 results)

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Sanctions follow PRC-01.1; 37 sanctions were applied in 2025 for privacy and security violations.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Position descriptions for ECIS roles include security duties.
Risk assessment standard STD-01.1 applies.
The ECIS is categorized High (section 6), reviewed annually.
The enterprise risk analysis (P01) covers the ECIS and is updated annually and after major changes.
Authenticated scans run weekly on ECIS servers. Gap: 5 of 60 sampled critical findings on presentation servers passed the 15-day remediation standard (POAM-017).
Risk responses are tracked in the register and POA&M.
Critical components (database servers, integration engine, identity) are identified in the BIA and protected with redundancy and monitoring.
STD-01.3 third-party security standard applies to ECIS acquisitions.
The ECIS security budget is part of the IT capital and operating plan.
EHR build follows the vendor's development life cycle and the system's validation plan.
Contracts for ECIS components include security, BAA, breach notice, and SBOM and vulnerability disclosure terms for medical device and software vendors.
Vendor security and administration guides are kept in the ECIS documentation library.
Design follows defense in depth: separated tiers, no direct database access from clients, encrypted channels.
External services supporting the ECIS are tiered and reviewed. Gap: 41 tier-1 and tier-2 vendors with PHI are overdue for reassessment, including 3 that connect to the integration engine (POAM-014).
Build and code changes are version-controlled with migration records.
The EHR vendor provides release security test summaries; the system tests portal and API releases with application scanning.
Upgrade and build standards are documented and reviewed with the vendor annually.
The EHR vendor trains the system's builders and analysts before certification to build.

control_name: Developer Security and Privacy Architecture and Design
implementation_statement: The vendor's security architecture is documented for the hosted components; documentation for the integration engine plug-ins from two smaller vendors is incomplete.
Vendor staff with access to ECIS data are screened by their employer under contract terms.

Unsupported components are tracked; the ECIS servers are supported. About 2,600 networked devices across the system run unsupported operating systems, some of which feed the ECIS, and deviations are not documented for all of them (POAM-009).
evidence: EV-012 (unsupported component list); EV-SA-22 (P07 SA-22 results)

implementation_statement: Encryption standard STD-04.1 and network standards apply.

control_name: Separation of System and User Functionality
implementation_statement: User functions are separated from database and system administration through separate tiers and accounts.
Security functions (identity, logging agents, backups) run on separate hosts or accounts from the EHR application.
Shared resources are cleared between sessions. Gap: Part 2 records from H-03 are not consistently flagged, so some appear in shared clinical views without the Part 2 notice (POAM-021).
The portal and API front end sit behind cloud DDoS protection and a web application firewall (CCP-07 with CCP-05).

ECIS tiers are segmented in both data centers; hospital networks reach the ECIS only through defined paths. Gap: H-08 reaches the integration engine over a legacy site VPN with broad access lists (POAM-006).
Client, interface, and API traffic is encrypted with TLS. HL7 over MLLP inside the data center integration segment is unencrypted under exception EXC-2026-031 (segmented, monitored; R-059).
Traffic between hospitals, data centers, and clouds runs over encrypted SD-WAN and private links.
Remote and gateway sessions terminate after 15 minutes of inactivity.
Keys for database and backup encryption are managed in key management services with rotation and separation of duties.
Cryptography uses FIPS-validated modules where available (TLS 1.2 or higher; AES-256 at rest).
Cameras and microphones on clinical workstations are off by default and show an indicator when used for telehealth.
Certificates come from the enterprise PKI and approved public authorities.
Mobile code (macros, scripts) is restricted on ECIS endpoints by policy.
External DNS zones are signed.

control_name: Secure Name/Address Resolution Service (Recursive or Caching Resolver)
implementation_statement: Internal resolvers validate DNS responses.

control_name: Architecture and Provisioning for Name/Address Resolution Service
implementation_statement: DNS services are redundant across both data centers.
Session identifiers are protected by TLS and invalidated at sign-out.
Interfaces queue messages and the database stops accepting writes rather than accepting partial transactions when a tier fails.
EHR databases, reporting replicas, backups, and BCA caches are encrypted at rest.
Storage encryption uses platform keys controlled by the system.
Each EHR process runs in its own execution domain on the server operating system.
System and information integrity procedures in STD-04.4 apply.
Servers and workstations are patched under STD-01.5 (critical within 15 days). Gap: patch SLA misses on EHR presentation servers (see RA-5; POAM-017).
EDR runs on all ECIS servers and endpoints with central monitoring.
The SOC monitors ECIS servers, identity, and network traffic 24x7. Gaps: medical device gateways and building OT networks are not fully monitored, and H-08 has no SIEM feeds (POAM-007).
evidence: EV-021 (SIEM coverage report); EV-SI-4 (P07 SI-4 results)

implementation_statement: Network detection monitors inbound and outbound traffic at the data center edges for unusual flows.
Threat intelligence from the health sector information sharing organization and CISA advisories is reviewed daily.
Security functions (audit, EDR, backup agents) report health daily; failures open tickets.

File integrity monitoring runs on ECIS servers, and build migrations are logged. Gap: interface errors that file results to the wrong encounter are detected only by user report; automated reconciliation is not in place (POAM-013).
evidence: EV-058 (FIM reports); EV-059 (incident records); EV-SI-7 (P07 SI-7 results)

implementation_statement: Integrity checks run daily on server binaries and weekly on the EHR build baseline.
Email filtering blocks spam and malicious attachments for all workforce mailboxes.
The integration engine validates message structure and patient identifiers; invalid messages go to an error queue reviewed every shift.
Error messages to users do not reveal system details.
Medical records are retained at least 5 years (482.24(b)(1)) and longer where state law requires; security documentation is kept 6 years.
Server operating systems use memory protection features (data execution prevention and address randomization).
Supply chain risk management is part of STD-01.3.
The supply chain risk management plan covers the EHR vendor, integration engine vendors, and medical device manufacturers.
Supply chain controls include vendor tiering, contract terms, and SBOM requests for tier-1 software and devices.
Acquisition strategy favors vendors with secure development attestations and coordinated vulnerability disclosure.
Supplier assessments run on a tier-based cycle; 41 tier-1 and tier-2 vendors are overdue (POAM-014).
BAAs and contracts require breach and security incident notice; tier-1 vendors must notify within 72 hours of a security incident affecting the system's data.
Tamper-evident seals for BCA computers and data center spares are planned for 2027 Q1.
Inspection of new ECIS hardware on receipt is planned with the 2027 server refresh.
Hardware and devices are bought only from manufacturers or authorized resellers.
ECIS components are disposed of through the certified sanitization vendor (MP-6).
